## Welcome!

Hello! I'm Hassan Maghfuri, a Registered Respiratory Therapist (RRT) and a graduate student pursuing a Master of Science in Biomedical and Health Informatics at Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland, Ohio.

I earned my Bachelor of Science in Respiratory Therapy from Indiana University of Pennsylvania in May 2024, graduating with a GPA of 3.90/4.00. After completing my undergraduate degree, I worked as a Registered Respiratory Therapist at Allegheny General Hospital in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, from November 2024 to July 2025. During this time, I gained over 1,500 hours of bedside experience caring for critically ill patients.

Working in critical care helped me develop an appreciation for the importance of clinical decision-making, accurate information, and communication among healthcare professionals. It also encouraged me to explore how technology and data can improve the way healthcare is delivered.

I began my graduate studies at Case Western Reserve University in Spring 2026. Through my coursework, I have been developing skills in statistical analysis, programming, machine learning, epidemiology, and geographic information systems.

My goal is to combine my clinical experience with biomedical informatics and data science to help improve patient care and healthcare decision-making.

## Academic Projects and Technical Skills

My graduate coursework has introduced me to several areas of healthcare research and technology.

**Artificial Intelligence in Medicine**

Using Python and TensorFlow to explore machine learning, neural networks, and classification methods.

**Statistical Analysis**

Using R, RStudio, and Quarto for data cleaning, exploratory analysis, statistical modeling, and reproducible reporting.

**Epidemiology**

Studying research designs, measures of disease occurrence, risk estimation, bias, and the interpretation of population health research.

**Geographic Information Systems**

Using ArcGIS to analyze and visualize geographic patterns in public health data.

## Professional Interests

I am interested in how clinical experience, biomedical informatics, artificial intelligence, and statistical analysis can work together to improve healthcare.

Having worked directly with patients in critical care, I understand the importance of accurate clinical information and timely decisions. I hope to use my experience in respiratory therapy alongside my graduate education to contribute to research and data-driven improvements in patient care.
